claims.text: The starting material is a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix without solid-lubricant additions.
Nanoscale h-BN particles can be uniformly incorporated into CoCrFeNi by powder metallurgy and spark plasma sintering.
Dispersed h-BN particles will facilitate formation of a continuous tribofilm on the sliding surface.
The h-BN-derived tribofilm will adhere to the sliding surface.
h-BN has a lamellar structure that can provide lubrication during sliding.
h-BN is sufficiently thermally stable to operate throughout sliding tests up to 800 °C.
Formation of an h-BN-containing lubricious film will reduce local interfacial shear stress.
Reduced local shear stress will lower the coefficient of friction.
The lubricious film will mitigate wear, including at elevated temperature.
The h-BN-reinforced composite will have a lower coefficient of friction than unreinforced CoCrFeNi from room temperature through 800 °C.
The h-BN-reinforced composite will have a lower wear rate than unreinforced CoCrFeNi from room temperature through 800 °C.
Unreinforced CoCrFeNi exhibits particularly high friction at elevated temperatures.
Unreinforced CoCrFeNi exhibits particularly high wear at elevated temperatures.
Tribofilm effectiveness depends on the quality of h-BN dispersion in the CoCrFeNi matrix.
Tribofilm effectiveness depends on interfacial bonding between h-BN and the CoCrFeNi matrix.
Processing parameters can alter h-BN dispersion and interfacial bonding.
Performance is proposed for sliding between room temperature and 800 °C under high loads in an inert or low-oxidation atmosphere.
A controlled comparison will use identically processed unreinforced CoCrFeNi and CoCrFeNi containing approximately 5 vol% nanoscale h-BN.
The comparison will measure friction and wear at room temperature, 400 °C, and 800 °C.
The hypothesis is falsified if the reinforced samples fail to show statistically significant reductions in both friction coefficient and wear rate across all tested temperatures.
